interpretation_rule: FORMAL evidence means the nurpa treats the concept as part of grammar/poetics or an explicit classified category. It must not be converted automatically into a historical claim about a Sangam poem.

dimensions.note: Akam/Puram and their relation are formal poetic domains.
Tiṇai and tuṟai are explicitly defined as structural poetic categories.
Land is part of mutal; landscape associations are formalized in Akattinai.
Time/season is part of mutal and landscape-time associations are explicit.
Plant/tree/flower categories occur in karu and are lexically classified in Marabiyal.
Animals/birds occur in karu; Marabiyal gives extensive age/sex/animal-name classifications.
Pastoralists, hunters, rulers, performers, household actors and status roles are formal categories.
Union, separation, waiting, lament, quarrel and household/lover relations are systematized.
Meyppattiyal and Akam rules directly classify emotion and lived states.
Pastoral/hunting roles, agriculture, royal service and commerce are explicitly treated.
Food is a karu category; Marabiyal explicitly mentions food classes and plough-based subsistence.
Dress/adornment behaviors and role-linked ornaments/regalia occur in formal rules.
Ritual implements, regalia, weapons and transport equipment are assigned to roles/categories.
Purattinai structurally classifies raid, march, siege and battle; weapon categories also occur in Marabiyal.
Sea travel, chariot/elephant/horse travel and military movement are explicit.
Fort, settlement, household, village/neighbourhood and camp contexts occur in formal poetic rules.
Wealth, poverty, gifts, possession, livelihood and role-linked resources are explicit.
Commerce is explicitly named as வாணிக வாழ்க்கை and gift/exchange contexts are formalized; the trade taxonomy is comparatively narrow.
Kingship, rulership, royal objects, warfare, counsel and public praise are systematic.
Kudi/group/status/class and occupation-linked social categories are explicitly grammaticalized.
Gender, mother/father/child/spouse/friend/nurse and kin roles are systematic.
Landscape deities, Velan/Korravai, hero-stone rites, blessings and divine fear/praise are explicit.
Kañci and hero-stone sequences formalize death, widowhood, lament, battle loss and memorialization.
Yāḻ, drum, song, dancer, bard, virali and poetic performance are explicit.
Grammar, phonology, poetics, textual method, cognition and scholarly procedure are pervasive formal subjects.
Aṟam, love, shame, chastity, generosity, blame/praise, truth/falsehood and other values are formalized.
Articulation anatomy, disease, ageing, bodily wasting, hunger, pallor and sleep loss are explicit.
Tolkāppiyam formalizes name-use constraints and includes named deity labels, but it is not a historical entity-resolution catalogue.
Poetic/textual forms, first/derivative texts, translation, commentary and scholarly comparison are formally described.
